1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# freeze.sh — cycle-130 ablation suite freeze (SDD §5.13, DEC-0404, DEC-0414)
     4	#
     5	# Writes or verifies <root>/MANIFEST.sha256, the suite's frozen identity: one
     6	# "<sha256>  <relpath>" line per file under <root>/tasks/ (and <root>/smoke/
     7	# with --smoke), relpath relative to the root, LC_ALL=C sorted, sha256 (Python
     8	# hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code, eval.yml trust boundary).
     9	# validate-suite.sh runs first; an invalid suite is never frozen or accepted.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   freeze.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--check] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
    13	#
    14	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0)
    15	#   --smoke           cover smoke/ too (passed to the validator as well)
    16	#   --check           recompute and compare with MANIFEST.sha256; write nothing
    17	#   --allow-partial   passed to validate-suite.sh (fewer than four tasks per type)
    18	#   --suite-file F    passed to validate-suite.sh
    19	#
    20	# Output: `freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 (N files, sha256 <digest of the manifest>)`
    21	# or `freeze: OK — N files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 …)`; on drift every
    22	# changed / added / removed path on its own line.
    23	#
    24	# Exit: 0 written / matches; 1 drift, missing manifest under --check, or the
    25	#       validator found violations; 2 usage.
    26	# Tested by evals/tests/freeze.bats.
    27	# =============================================================================
    28	set -euo pipefail
    29	export LC_ALL=C
    30	
    31	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    32	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    33	
    34	ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
    35	CHECK=false SMOKE=false
    36	VARGS=()
    37	
    38	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,26p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    39	die() { echo "freeze: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    40	
    41	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    42	  case "$1" in
    43	    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    44	    --smoke) SMOKE=true; VARGS+=(--smoke); shift ;;
    45	    --check) CHECK=true; shift ;;
    46	    --allow-partial) VARGS+=(--allow-partial); shift ;;
    47	    --suite-file) [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] || die "--suite-file needs a path"; VARGS+=(--suite-file "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    48	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    49	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    50	  esac
    51	done
    52	[[ -n "$ROOT" && -d "$ROOT" ]] || die "suite root not found: ${ROOT:-<empty>}"
    53	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"
    54	MANIFEST="$ROOT/MANIFEST.sha256"
    55	
    56	vrc=0
    57	"$SCRIPT_DIR/validate-suite.sh" --root "$ROOT" ${VARGS[@]+"${VARGS[@]}"} || vrc=$?
    58	if [[ $vrc -eq 1 ]]; then echo "freeze: refused — the suite does not validate" >&2; exit 1; fi
    59	[[ $vrc -eq 0 ]] || die "validate-suite.sh failed (exit $vrc)"
    60	
    61	# compute_manifest <out> — the manifest body for the current tree.
    62	compute_manifest() {
    63	  local out="$1" list dirs=(tasks)
    64	  [[ "$SMOKE" == "true" ]] && dirs+=(smoke)
    65	  list="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze-list.XXXXXX")"
    66	  local d
    67	  for d in "${dirs[@]}"; do
    68	    [[ -d "$ROOT/$d" ]] || continue
    69	    ( cd "$ROOT" && find "$d" -type f -print )
    70	  done | LC_ALL=C sort > "$list"
    71	  if grep -q '\\' "$list"; then rm -f "$list"; die "a path under the suite holds a backslash"; fi
    72	  python3 -I - "$ROOT" "$list" > "$out" <<'PY' || { rm -f "$list"; die "hashing failed"; }
    73	import hashlib, os, sys
    74	root, listing = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    75	for rel in open(listing, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines():
    76	    if not rel:
    77	        continue
    78	    h = hashlib.sha256()
    79	    with open(os.path.join(root, rel), "rb") as f:
    80	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
    81	            h.update(b)
    82	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + rel)
    83	PY
    84	  rm -f "$list"
    85	}
    86	digest_of() { python3 -I -c 'import hashlib, sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$1"; }
    87	
    88	TMP="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/freeze.XXXXXX")"

    90	compute_manifest "$TMP"

    96	    echo "freeze: OK — $n files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 $(digest_of "$MANIFEST"))"
    97	    exit 0
    98	  fi
    99	  echo "freeze: DRIFT against $MANIFEST:"
   100	  python3 -I - "$MANIFEST" "$TMP" <<'PY'
   101	import sys
   102	def load(p):
   103	    m = {}
   104	    for line in open(p, encoding="utf-8"):
   105	        line = line.rstrip("\n")
   106	        if line:
   107	            h, _, rel = line.partition("  ")
   108	            m[rel] = h
   109	    return m
   110	old, new = load(sys.argv[1]), load(sys.argv[2])
   111	for rel in sorted(set(old) | set(new)):
   112	    if rel not in new:
   113	        print(f"  removed  {rel}")
   114	    elif rel not in old:
   115	        print(f"  added    {rel}")
   116	    elif old[rel] != new[rel]:
   117	        print(f"  changed  {rel}")
   118	PY
   119	  exit 1
   120	fi
   121	
   122	cp "$TMP" "$MANIFEST.tmp" && mv "$MANIFEST.tmp" "$MANIFEST"
   123	echo "freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 ($n files, sha256 $(digest_of "$MANIFEST"))"
   124	exit 0
   125	#!/usr/bin/env bash
   126	# =============================================================================
   127	# fingerprint.sh — toolchain fingerprint for ablation runs (cycle-130 FR-4, SDD A11 / DEC-0389)
   128	#
   129	# Prints `fp:<sha256>` over the LC_ALL=C-sorted `tool=version` lines of the
   130	# toolchain an ablation run depends on (claude, codex, python3, node, yq, jq,
   131	# bats, git, docker) plus `source_tree=<HEAD of --source-tree>`. A tool that is
   132	# not installed reads `tool=absent`, so a missing tool changes the fingerprint
   133	# instead of failing the run. The value fills `image_digest` in host mode and
   134	# `fingerprint` in every mode (MANIFEST.json, pipeline.json, runs.jsonl). It reads the
   135	# HOST toolchain: in container mode the phases run on the image's toolchain, and the
   136	# image digest (not this value) identifies the batch's versions (on 2026-10-15 the host
   137	# CLI was 2.1.300 while Dockerfile.ablation pins 2.1.299).
   138	#
   139	# Usage:
   140	#   fingerprint.sh [--source-tree DIR] [--claude-bin B] [--bats-bin B] [--json]
   141	#
   142	# Options:
   143	#   --source-tree DIR  the pinned Loa tree; its `git rev-parse HEAD` is folded in
   144	#                      (`none` when absent or not a git tree)
   145	#   --claude-bin B     the CLI executable (default: $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
   146	#   --bats-bin B       bats executable (default: bats on PATH, else the operator's
   147	#                      ~/.local/dotfiles/tools/diff-so-fancy/test/bats/bin/bats)
   148	#   --json             print {fingerprint, tools{}, source_tree, lines[]} instead
   149	#
   150	# Exit codes:
   151	#   0  printed
   152	#   2  usage error
   153	#
   154	# Tested by evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats (fingerprint cases).
   155	# =============================================================================
   156	set -euo pipefail
   157	export LC_ALL=C
   158	
   159	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
   160	# "Validate grader trust boundary").
   161	
   162	SOURCE_TREE=""
   163	CLAUDE_BIN="${EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN:-claude}"
   164	BATS_BIN="${LOA_EVAL_BATS_BIN:-}"
   165	JSON=false
   166	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
   167	  case "$1" in
   168	    --source-tree) SOURCE_TREE="${2:?--source-tree needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   169	    --claude-bin)  CLAUDE_BIN="${2:?--claude-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   170	    --bats-bin)    BATS_BIN="${2:?--bats-bin needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
   171	    --json)        JSON=true; shift ;;
   172	    -h|--help)     sed -n '2,28p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;

   179	fi
   180	
   181	# first line of `<bin> <args>`, whitespace collapsed; `absent` when not runnable

   195	    printf 'codex=%s\n'   "$(tool_version codex --version)"
   196	    printf 'python3=%s\n' "$(tool_version python3 --version)"
   197	    printf 'node=%s\n'    "$(tool_version node --version)"
   198	    printf 'yq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version yq --version)"
   199	    printf 'jq=%s\n'      "$(tool_version jq --version)"

   201	    printf 'git=%s\n'     "$(tool_version git --version)"
   202	    printf 'docker=%s\n'  "$(tool_version docker --version)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# validate-suite.sh — cycle-130 ablation task-suite validator (SDD §3.2, DEC-0424)
     4	#
     5	# Checks every task of the ablation-2.0 suite before it is frozen, run or graded.
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   validate-suite.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
     9	#
    10	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0); the
    11	#                     tasks are <root>/tasks/<id>/task.yaml
    12	#   --smoke           also validate <root>/smoke/<id>/task.yaml (never counted)
    13	#   --allow-partial   skip the four-by-four type count (Sprint 258 state)
    14	#   --suite-file F    suite yaml (default evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml): arm ids
    15	#                     for the leakage check, arms' task_types, suite_version
    16	#
    17	# Checks (each violation is one stdout line `<task-id>: <reason>`):
    18	#   1. schema: id (= directory name), schema_version 1, type (feature-build |
    19	#      bug-fix | refactor | review-catch), source {kind, date, fix_commit?,
    20	#      base_commit?, bead?, origin?}, post_cutoff (bool), fixture (dir under the
    21	#      root; null only for review-catch), criterion (agent-facing; no path, file
    22	#      name or test name), success_criterion, test_command (array; null only for
    23	#      review-catch), regression_command (array | null), reference_patch (hidden/…
    24	#      | null; required for bug-fix and feature-build), grader_protected (array of
    25	#      relative paths present in the fixture), structural_check (hidden/… | null;
    26	#      required for refactor), bounds {max_turns{}, timeout_min{}} (phase → positive
    27	#      int), review_catch (null, or {fixture, manifest, labels?} for review-catch,
    28	#      both present), suite_version (= the suite file's), TASK.md present
    29	#   2. counts: four tasks of each type under tasks/ (unless --allow-partial)
    30	#   3. allowlist: test_command[0] and regression_command[0] in python3 | pytest |
    31	#      bats | bash | node | npx
    32	#   4. hidden/manifest.json (build types): {"files": [{src, dest}]}; every src
    33	#      exists under hidden/; every dest is relative, inside the tree, no `..`
    34	#   5. fixture path rule (build types): check_fixture_path_rule from
    35	#      lib/sandbox-mount.sh — no .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/
    36	#      or .run/ at the fixture's top level; the reference patch touches none either
    37	#   6. leakage: TASK.md and criterion (the task-brief text is built from these)
    38	#      and every phase prompt under evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts/ contain none
    39	#      of: the string `hidden` (any case), a hidden test file's stem, a defect id
    40	#      of the review manifest, a `D[0-9]{2}-` key, an arm id of the suite file
    41	#   7. suite file: every non-absent arm's task_types are known (all | build |

   157	def leak_scan(tid, label, text, stems, defect_ids):

1	# =============================================================================
     2	# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
     3	#
     4	# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
     5	# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
     6	# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
     7	# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
     8	#
     9	# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
    10	# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
    11	# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
    12	# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
    13	# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
    14	# task_types against the known types).
    15	#
    16	# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
    17	#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
    18	#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
    19	# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
    20	#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
    21	#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
    22	# =============================================================================
    23	name: ablation-2.0
    24	version: 1
    25	source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
    26	agy_opt_in: false

    34	caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
    35	priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
    36	cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)

    39	# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
    40	phase_defaults:
    41	  models:
    42	    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
     6	# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
     7	# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
     8	# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
     9	# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
    10	# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
    11	#
    12	#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
    13	#
    14	# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
    15	# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
    16	# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
    17	#
    18	#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
    19	#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
    20	#
    21	# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
    22	# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
    23	# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
    24	# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
    28	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
    32	#                the current directory)
    33	#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
    34	#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
    35	#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
    36	#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
    37	#   -h, --help   this text
    38	#
    39	# Exit codes:
    40	#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
    41	#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
    42	#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
    43	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
    44	#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
    45	# =============================================================================
    46	set -euo pipefail
    47	export LC_ALL=C
    48	
    49	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    50	# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
    51	source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    52	
    53	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    54	die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    55	
    56	MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
    57	ROOT=""
    58	OUT=""
    59	CHECK=0
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
    63	    --root)
    64	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    65	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --out)
    67	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
    68	      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    69	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    70	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    71	  esac
    72	done
    73	
    74	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    75	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    76	fi
    77	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    78	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    79	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    80	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    81	[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || OUT="${ROOT}/${MANIFEST_REL}"
    82	
    83	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gen-checksums.XXXXXX")"
    84	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    85	trap cleanup EXIT
    86	
    87	# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
    88	files=()
    89	while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
    90	  case "$path" in
    91	    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
    92	  esac
    93	  case "$path" in
    94	    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
    95	  esac
    96	  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
    97	    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
    98	    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
    99	    continue
   100	  fi
   101	  files+=("$path")
   102	done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)
   103	
   104	# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
   105	TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
   106	: > "$TSV"
   107	n=${#files[@]}
   108	i=0
   109	while [[ $i -lt $n ]]; do
   110	  chunk=("${files[@]:i:400}")
   111	  hashes=()
   112	  while IFS= read -r line; do
   113	    hashes+=("${line%% *}")
   114	  done < <(cd "$ROOT" && sha256_portable "${chunk[@]}")
   115	  [[ ${#hashes[@]} -eq ${#chunk[@]} ]] || die2 "sha256 returned ${#hashes[@]} digests for ${#chunk[@]} paths"
   116	  j=0
   117	  while [[ $j -lt ${#chunk[@]} ]]; do
   118	    [[ "${hashes[j]}" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]] || die2 "unexpected sha256 output for ${chunk[j]}"
   119	    printf '%s\t%s\n' "${chunk[j]}" "${hashes[j]}" >> "$TSV"
   120	    j=$((j + 1))
   121	  done
   122	  i=$((i + 400))
   123	done
   124	[[ $n -gt 0 ]] || echo "gen-checksums: warning: no tracked files under .claude in $ROOT" >&2
   125	
   126	GEN="${TMP_DIR}/checksums.json"
   127	jq -Rn --arg generated "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '
   128	  {generated: $generated, algorithm: "sha256",
   129	   files: ([inputs | select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {key: .[0], value: .[1]}] | from_entries)}
   130	' < "$TSV" > "$GEN"
   131	
   132	# --- 3a. write ----------------------------------------------------------------
   133	if [[ $CHECK -eq 0 ]]; then
   134	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
   135	  chmod 0644 "$GEN"
   136	  # mv replaces a symlinked manifest instead of writing through it.
   137	  mv -f "$GEN" "$OUT"
   138	  echo "gen-checksums: wrote $n entries to $OUT" >&2
   139	  exit 0
   140	fi
   141	
   142	# --- 3b. --check --------------------------------------------------------------
   143	if [[ ! -f "$OUT" ]]; then
   144	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest not found: $OUT (run tools/gen-checksums.sh)" >&2
   145	  exit 1
   146	fi
   147	if ! jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$OUT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   148	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: manifest is not JSON with a files object: $OUT" >&2
   149	  exit 1
   150	fi
   151	DIFF="${TMP_DIR}/diff.txt"
   152	jq -rn --slurpfile old "$OUT" --slurpfile new "$GEN" '
   153	  ($old[0].files) as $o | ($new[0].files) as $n |
   154	  ( [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select($o | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "added"} ]
   155	  + [ $o | keys[] | . as $p | select($n | has($p) | not) | {p: $p, k: "removed"} ]
   156	  + [ $n | keys[] | . as $p | select(($o | has($p)) and $o[$p] != $n[$p]) | {p: $p, k: "changed"} ] )
   157	  | sort_by(.p) | .[] | "\(.k): \(.p)"
   158	' > "$DIFF"
   159	count=$(wc -l < "$DIFF" | tr -d ' ')
   160	if [[ "$count" -eq 0 ]]; then
   161	  echo "gen-checksums: --check: OK ($n entries match $OUT)" >&2
   162	  exit 0
   163	fi
   164	echo "gen-checksums: --check: DRIFT — $count path(s) differ between $OUT and the tracked tree:" >&2
   165	sed -n '1,10s/^/  /p' "$DIFF" >&2
   166	[[ "$count" -le 10 ]] || echo "  ... and $((count - 10)) more" >&2
   167	echo "gen-checksums: regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   168	exit 1

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
     6	# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
     7	# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
     8	# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
     9	# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
    10	#
    11	# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
    12	#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
    13	#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
    14	#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
    15	#                      (a path component of that name)
    16	#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
    17	#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
    18	#                  other
    19	#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
    20	# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
    21	# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
    22	#
    23	# Last line on stdout:
    24	#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
    28	#
    29	# Options:
    30	#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
    31	#                    current directory)
    32	#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
    33	#   -h, --help       this text
    34	#
    35	# Exit codes:
    36	#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
    37	#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
    38	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
    39	#      not JSON with a `files` object
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	
    47	ROOT=""
    48	MANIFEST=""
    49	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    50	  case "$1" in
    51	    --root)
    52	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    53	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    54	    --manifest)
    55	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
    56	      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    57	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    58	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    59	  esac
    60	done
    61	
    62	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    63	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    64	fi
    65	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    66	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    67	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    68	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    69	[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
    70	[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
    71	jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1 \

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
     4	#
     5	# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
     6	# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
     7	# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
     8	#
     9	# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
    10	#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
    11	#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
    12	#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
    13	#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
    14	#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
    15	#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
    16	#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
    17	#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
    18	#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
    19	#                    submodule from there; no network).
    20	#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
    21	#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
    22	#      is printed, then a summary line

    24	#
    25	# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
    26	# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
    27	# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
    28	#
    29	# Usage:
    30	#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]
    31	#
    32	# Options:
    33	#   --ref REF    commit-ish of this repository to mount (default: HEAD of the
    34	#                repository the script lives in)
    35	#   --worktree   mount REF plus the source work tree's uncommitted state

    37	#   --keep       keep the temp directory and print its path
    38	#   --tmp DIR    parent directory for the temp directory (default: $TMPDIR or
    39	#                /tmp)
    40	#   -h, --help   this text

    43	#   0    check-loa.sh exited 0 on the fresh mount

    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }

    56	REF=""
    57	KEEP=0
    58	WORKTREE=0
    59	TMP_PARENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"

    61	  case "$1" in

    64	      REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    65	    --tmp)
    66	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--tmp requires a directory"

   126	      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
   127	      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"

   129	      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
   130	    else
   131	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   132	    fi
   133	  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)

   135	  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"
   136	}

   139	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mounting upstream commit $MOUNT_SHA"

   142	DOWN="$WORK/downstream"

   144	init_downstream() {
   145	  git -C "$DOWN" init --quiet
   146	  printf '# downstream fixture\n' > "$DOWN/README.md"

   148	  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"
   149	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
     3	# =============================================================================
     4	# tests/unit/check-loa-mount-scope.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 #1267,
     5	# AC-1.2/AC-1.3; SDD §5.3). check-loa.sh check_integrity classifies every
     6	# manifest path as ok, Tampered (fail), not-mounted (a submodule mount does
     7	# not link it but .loa/<path> has it: counted, one summary line, never a
     8	# failure) or Missing (fail).
     9	#
    10	# Seam: check-loa.sh already guards `main` behind
    11	#   [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]
    12	# so each case sources the script in a child bash inside the fixture
    13	# directory and calls check_integrity alone; the child exits 1 when the
    14	# FAILURES counter is non-zero, the same rule main applies. No other check
    15	# runs, and the script is not modified for the test.
    16	# =============================================================================
    17	
    18	setup() {
    19	  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
    20	  CHECK="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh"
    21	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cloams.XXXXXX")"
    22	  D="$T/downstream"
    23	  # upstream tree inside the submodule path
    24	  mkdir -p "$D/.loa/.claude/lib" "$D/.claude"
    25	  printf 'echo a\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/a.sh"
    26	  printf 'echo b\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh"
    27	  printf 'echo c\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh"
    28	  # the mount links a.sh only (b.sh and lib/c.sh are not linked)
    29	  ln -s ../.loa/.claude/a.sh "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    30	  printf 'aleph:\n  enabled: false\n' > "$D/.loa.config.yaml"
    31	  source "$ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    32	  HA="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/a.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    33	  HB="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    34	  HC="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    35	  write_manifest
    36	}
    37	teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
    38	
    39	# write_manifest [extra-path hash]... — a/b/lib/c plus any extra pairs
    40	write_manifest() {
    41	  local args=(--arg a "$HA" --arg b "$HB" --arg c "$HC")
    42	  local filter='{".claude/a.sh": $a, ".claude/b.sh": $b, ".claude/lib/c.sh": $c}'
    43	  if [[ $# -ge 2 ]]; then
    44	    args+=(--arg xp "$1" --arg xh "$2")
    45	    filter="$filter + {(\$xp): \$xh}"
    46	  fi
    47	  jq -n "${args[@]}" "{generated: \"2026-10-15T00:00:00Z\", algorithm: \"sha256\", files: ($filter)}" \
    48	    > "$D/.claude/checksums.json"
    49	}
    50	
    51	run_integrity() {
    52	  run bash -c 'cd "$1" && source "$2" && check_integrity && echo "FAILURES=$FAILURES" && [[ $FAILURES -eq 0 ]]' \
    53	    _ "$D" "$CHECK"
    54	}
    55	
    56	@test "CM-1 paths in the upstream tree but not linked are not-mounted; exit unaffected" {
    57	  run_integrity
    58	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    59	  [[ "$output" == *"not-mounted: 2 path(s) exist in the upstream tree but are not linked by this mount"* ]]
    60	  [[ "$output" == *"Integrity verified"* ]]
    61	  [[ "$output" != *"Missing:"* ]]
    62	  [[ "$output" != *"Tampered:"* ]]
    63	  [ "$(grep -c 'not-mounted:' <<< "$output")" -eq 1 ]
    64	}
    65	
    66	@test "CM-2 a present file whose hash differs is Tampered and fails" {
    67	  rm -f "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    68	  printf 'echo tampered\n' > "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    69	  run_integrity
    70	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    71	  [[ "$output" == *"Tampered: .claude/a.sh"* ]]
    72	  [[ "$output" != *"Integrity verified"* ]]
    73	  [[ "$output" == *"FAILURES=1"* ]]
    74	}
    75	
    76	@test "CM-3 a path absent locally and upstream is Missing and fails" {
    77	  write_manifest .claude/gone.sh "$HA"
    78	  run_integrity
    79	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    80	  [[ "$output" == *"Missing: .claude/gone.sh"* ]]
    81	  [[ "$output" == *"not-mounted: 2 path(s)"* ]]
    82	  [[ "$output" != *"Integrity verified"* ]]
    83	}
    84	
    85	@test "CM-4 without a .loa/ submodule an absent path is Missing" {
    86	  find "$D/.loa" -mindepth 1 -delete
    87	  rmdir "$D/.loa"
    88	  printf 'echo a\n' > "$D/.claude/a.sh.real"
    89	  rm -f "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    90	  mv "$D/.claude/a.sh.real" "$D/.claude/a.sh"
    91	  run_integrity
    92	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    93	  [[ "$output" == *"Missing: .claude/b.sh"* ]]
    94	  [[ "$output" == *"Missing: .claude/lib/c.sh"* ]]
    95	  [[ "$output" != *"not-mounted"* ]]
    96	}
    97	
    98	@test "CM-5 every path linked and matching: Integrity verified, no not-mounted line" {
    99	  ln -s ../.loa/.claude/b.sh "$D/.claude/b.sh"
   100	  mkdir -p "$D/.claude/lib"
   101	  ln -s ../../.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh "$D/.claude/lib/c.sh"
   102	  run_integrity
   103	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   104	  [[ "$output" == *"Integrity verified"* ]]
   105	  [[ "$output" != *"not-mounted"* ]]
   106	}
   107	
   108	@test "CM-6 no checksums file: warn and skip, no failure" {
   109	  rm -f "$D/.claude/checksums.json"
   110	  run_integrity
   111	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   112	  [[ "$output" == *"No checksums file - skipping integrity check"* ]]
   113	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# evals/tests/spend.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.5 (PRD FR-2 AC-2.3, SDD §5.11)
     4	#
     5	# spend.sh sums run rows (cost_usd, each run_id once across files) and the cost
     6	# ledger (cost_micro_usd, ts >= since) and prints total, components, cap,
     7	# headroom and reserve. Fixtures: evals/tests/fixtures/ablation/spend/ —
     8	# runs.jsonl 6.41 + 3.59, rows.jsonl 3.59 (same run_id, counted once) + 2.00,
     9	# ledger 1.00 before the kickoff, 2.50 and 0.50 after it.
    10	# =============================================================================
    11	
    12	setup() {
    13	  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    14	  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    15	  SPEND="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/spend.sh"
    16	  FX="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation/spend"
    17	  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sp.XXXXXX")"
    18	}
    19	
    20	teardown() {
    21	  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
    22	  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
    23	}
    24	
    25	@test "SP-1 rows (deduplicated by run_id) plus ledger rows since the default kickoff: the summary line" {
    26	  run "$SPEND" --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" "$FX/rows.jsonl" --ledger "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl"
    27	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    28	  [ "$output" = "cycle spend USD 15.00 (runs 12.00 + ledger 3.00 since 2026-10-14T13:50:00Z); cap 1,500; headroom 1,485.00; reserve 250" ]
    29	}
    30	
    31	@test "SP-2 --json carries the same fields" {
    32	  run "$SPEND" --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" --runs "$FX/rows.jsonl" --ledger "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl" --json
    33	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    34	  [ "$(jq -r '.total_usd' <<<"$output")" = "15" ]
    35	  [ "$(jq -r '.runs_usd' <<<"$output")" = "12" ]
    36	  [ "$(jq -r '.ledger_usd' <<<"$output")" = "3" ]
    37	  [ "$(jq -r '.since' <<<"$output")" = "2026-10-14T13:50:00Z" ]
    38	  [ "$(jq -r '.cap_usd' <<<"$output")" = "1500" ]
    39	  [ "$(jq -r '.headroom_usd' <<<"$output")" = "1485" ]
    40	  [ "$(jq -r '.reserve_usd' <<<"$output")" = "250" ]
    41	  [ "$(jq -r '.runs_rows' <<<"$output")" = "3" ]
    42	  [ "$(jq -r '.runs_rows_deduped' <<<"$output")" = "1" ]
    43	  [ "$(jq -r '.ledger_rows' <<<"$output")" = "2" ]
    44	  [ "$(jq -r '.runs_files | length' <<<"$output")" = "2" ]
    45	}
    46	
    47	@test "SP-3 --since filters the ledger only (a date, a timestamp, the full history); --cap and --reserve override; headroom goes negative" {
    48	  run "$SPEND" --since 2026-10-15 --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" --ledger "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl" --json
    49	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    50	  [ "$(jq -r '.ledger_usd' <<<"$output")" = "0.5" ]
    51	  [ "$(jq -r '.runs_usd' <<<"$output")" = "10" ]
    52	  run "$SPEND" --since 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z --ledger "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl" --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" --cap 12 --reserve 3
    53	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    54	  [ "$output" = "cycle spend USD 14.00 (runs 10.00 + ledger 4.00 since 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z); cap 12; headroom -2.00; reserve 3" ]
    55	}
    56	
    57	@test "SP-4 a malformed line is skipped and counted; the rest still sums" {
    58	  { cat "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl"; echo '{not json'; echo '{"ts":"2026-10-15T02:00:00Z"}'; } > "$T/ledger.jsonl"
    59	  run "$SPEND" --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" --ledger "$T/ledger.jsonl" --json
    60	  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    61	  json="$(grep '^{' <<<"$output")"
    62	  [ "$(jq -r '.skipped_lines' <<<"$json")" = "1" ]
    63	  [ "$(jq -r '.ledger_usd' <<<"$json")" = "3" ]
    64	  [ "$(jq -r '.ledger_rows' <<<"$json")" = "3" ]
    65	}
    66	
    67	@test "SP-5 exit 1 on an unreadable file; exit 2 on usage errors" {
    68	  run "$SPEND" --runs "$T/absent.jsonl" --ledger "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl"
    69	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    70	  grep -q 'unreadable' <<<"$output"
    71	  run "$SPEND" --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" --ledger "$T/absent-ledger.jsonl"
    72	  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    73	  run "$SPEND" --since yesterday --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" --ledger "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl"
    74	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    75	  run "$SPEND" --cap -5 --runs "$FX/runs.jsonl" --ledger "$FX/cost-ledger.jsonl"
    76	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    77	  run "$SPEND" --runs
    78	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
    79	  run "$SPEND" --bogus
    80	  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]

        # cycle-110 sprint-2a T2.3 (SDD §3.2): auth_type + dispatch_group migration.
        auth_type: http_api
        dispatch_group: openai-gpt
        capabilities: [chat, tools, function_calling, code]
        context_window: 400000
        token_param: max_completion_tokens
        # cycle-104 Sprint 2 T2.3: within-company chain.
        fallback_chain:
          - openai:gpt-5.3-codex
          - openai:codex-headless
        endpoint_family: responses      # cycle-095 Sprint 1: gpt-5.5 only routes through /v1/responses
        # cycle-102 Sprint 1 T1.9: reasoning-class /v1/responses (closes A1).
        max_output_tokens: 32000
        # cycle-102 Sprint 1F: parity with gpt-5.5-pro input-size gate. Same
        # cheval HTTP-asymmetry failure mode (KF-002 layer 3).
        # Sprint 4A (cycle-102, AC-4.5e): streaming transport now defaults
        # on for openai_adapter._complete_streaming, eliminating the 60s
        # server-side disconnect class by construction. The gate stays as
        # belt-and-suspenders against future intermediary-timer regressions
        # AND against context-window overflow (well below 400K). Raised
        # from 24000 → 200000 to reflect streaming's actual safe range.
        # Operator override per-call: `--max-input-tokens N` (0 disables);
        # global: `LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_INPUT_GATE=1`. Kill streaming via
        # `LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING=1` to fall back to the legacy
        # non-streaming path (which still hits the original 24K wall).
        # cycle-103 Sprint 3 T3.4 / AC-3.4: split into streaming-default
        # vs legacy-fallback. When `LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING=1`, the
        # gate uses `legacy_max_input_tokens` automatically — operator no
        # longer has to manually lower the cap after killing streaming.
        max_input_tokens: 200000          # backward-compat fallback
        streaming_max_input_tokens: 200000
        legacy_max_input_tokens: 24000    # pre-Sprint-4A KF-002 wall
        # cycle-095 Sprint 2: probe_required dropped — gpt-5.5 is GA on /v1/models
        # since 2026-04-23. Probe-gated fail-fast still applies via the
        # generic AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE state in .run/model-health-cache.json
        # (see PRD G-7 + Sprint 1 probe_required clarification block in sprint.md).
        # Wire-protocol gate: OpenAI's Responses API for gpt-5.5 rejects the
        # `temperature` parameter with HTTP 400 ("Unsupported parameter:
        # 'temperature' is not supported with this model"). The cheval adapter
        # at .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py consults
        # `params.temperature_supported` per request and omits the field when
        # False (mirrors the claude-opus-4-7 #641 pattern). Verified
        # 2026-05-07 via direct curl to /v1/responses.
        params:
          temperature_supported: false
        pricing:
          input_per_mtok: 5000000       # $5.00 per million tokens (confirmed 2026-04-29)
          output_per_mtok: 30000000     # $30.00 per million tokens (output_tokens INCLUSIVE of reasoning_tokens; SDD §5.5)
      gpt-6.1-sol:
        # cycle-130 Sprint 258 (2026-10-15): the model Codex on a ChatGPT plan
        # serves by default after it withdrew every gpt-5.x name (KF-044); the
        # codex-headless hop's cli_model points here so its estimates price
        # through this entry. Listed by /v1/models with the operator's key.
        # Shape mirrored from gpt-5.5 (400K window, /v1/responses, 32K out).
        auth_type: http_api
        dispatch_group: openai-gpt
        capabilities: [chat, tools, function_calling, code]
        context_window: 400000
        token_param: max_completion_tokens
        # within-company chain, terminating in the CLI hop as every OpenAI primary does
        fallback_chain:
          - openai:codex-headless
        endpoint_family: responses
        max_output_tokens: 32000
        max_input_tokens: 200000
        streaming_max_input_tokens: 200000
        legacy_max_input_tokens: 24000
        params:
          temperature_supported: false
        pricing:
          # PLACEHOLDER: gpt-5.5 list prices copied 2026-10-15 until the gpt-6.1
          # rate card is confirmed (bead at the Sprint 258 close). The codex
          # hop itself bills the operator's subscription; this entry prices
          # estimates and MODELINV rows only.
          input_per_mtok: 5000000       # $5.00 per million tokens (placeholder, see above)
          output_per_mtok: 30000000     # $30.00 per million tokens (placeholder, see above)
      gpt-5.5-pro:
        capabilities: [chat, code]      # No tools, no structured_json
        # #881 close, #914 F-001 correction: declare the real per-CLI context
        # window so cheval's enforce_context_window does not pull the 128000-
        # token global default (loa_cheval/types.py:107). The codex CLI
        # dispatches gpt-5.5 by default — matches the http_api gpt-5.5 entry
        # in this file (context_window: 400000). The initial PR shipped
        # 200000 with an inaccurate comment claiming gpt-5.5 was 200000;
        # corrected post-BB review to the real 400000 capacity.
        context_window: 400000
        # No pricing entry — CLI uses operator's Codex subscription.
        # cycle-104 sprint-2 T2.11 amendment: cli_model is the model
        # passed to `codex exec --model <name>`. The CLI doesn't
        # recognize the Loa alias; this maps to the real codex model.
        # cycle-130 Sprint 258 (2026-10-15): Codex on a ChatGPT plan no longer
        # serves any gpt-5.x name (HTTP 400 "not supported when using Codex
        # with a ChatGPT account" for gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.5-codex,
        # gpt-5.3-codex; codex 0.137 and 0.162 alike). The CLI's own default
        # is gpt-6.1-sol, which answers; the HTTP gpt-5.5 entries above are
        # unchanged (the API still lists them). Recorded as KF-044.
        extra:
          cli_model: gpt-6.1-sol

# Copy of evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml as implementer B landed it (Sprint 258); the fixture runs and
# evals/tests/{pipeline-run,ablation-row,took-effect}.bats read this copy so the tests do not move with the live suite.
# =============================================================================
# evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml — cycle-130 Loa 2.0 component ablation suite
#
# SDD §3.3 (structure reproduced), extended by Sprint 258 Task 1.6: the
# tasks block with the smoke root, phase_defaults, phase_sets, cost_hint, each
# arm's phase-set override and took-effect rule ids, and the full pre-registered
# rules block (D-A5; mirrored in NOTES before the first run, DEC-0383).
#
# Readers: execute-agent.sh / lib/sandbox-mount.sh (arms[].toggles via
# resolve_arm_toggles), pipeline-run.sh (phase_defaults, phase_sets,
# arms[].phases, arms[].effort), took-effect.sh (arms[].took_effect),
# run-ablation.sh (trials, caps, priority, cut_ladder, arms[].task_types),
# ablation-report.py (rules), validate-suite.sh (arm ids for the leakage check,
# task_types against the known types).
#
# task_types: `all` | `build` (= feature-build, bug-fix, refactor) |
#   `review-catch` | a single build type. An arm is never scheduled, and a row
#   never reported, on a type outside its declaration (DEC-0400, DEC-0406).
# took_effect: rule ids took-effect.sh evaluates per trial (DEC-0418); a miss is
#   infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. `applicability_refused` is the
#   smoke's evidence line that the planner refused the arm on a review-catch task.
# =============================================================================
name: ablation-2.0
version: 1
source_commit: "<sprint-258-commit>"   # the lead sets the Sprint 258 commit (rc.5 plus the mount fix; F2, DEC-0392)
agy_opt_in: false
tasks:
  root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/tasks
  manifest: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/MANIFEST.sha256
  smoke_root: grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke
suite_version: 1
trials: {build: 3, review-catch: 3}      # D-A4: review-catch trials 3, not 5, under the gate pipeline
cut_ladder: ["A5, A6, A7 not run", "A2 and A3 build trials 3 -> 2", "A3 review-catch trials 3 -> 2"]   # DEC-0397; A0, A1, A4 keep 3
caps: {cycle_usd: 1500, run_usd: 12, reserve_usd: 250}   # reserve released to A7 when the re-verification rule needs no run (DEC-0398)
priority: [a0_bare, a1_full, a2_no_sprint_plan, a3_one_voice, a4_no_gates, a7_effort_medium, a5_no_flatline, a6_one_window]
cost_hint: {build: 7, review-catch: 8}   # USD per run before any actual exists (run-arms/run-ablation est_next fallback)

# Session defaults per phase (SDD D-4.3). A6's continued session carries the
# caps of the phase it is in; A0's BARE caps are PLAN + IMPLEMENT + 2 x FIX.
phase_defaults:
  models:
    PLAN: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    IMPLEMENT: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    FIX: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    BARE: global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5
    REVIEW: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
    AUDIT: global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1
  max_turns: {PLAN: 30, IMPLEMENT: 60, REVIEW: 40, FIX: 40, AUDIT: 40, BARE: 170}
  timeout_min: {PLAN: 15, IMPLEMENT: 25, REVIEW: 20, FIX: 15, AUDIT: 20, BARE: 70}
  tools: "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Edit,Task,WebFetch"   # identical for every arm, A0 included
phase_sets:   # D-4.1: A1's phases per task type; FIX runs only after a CHANGES_REQUIRED gate
  review-catch: [REVIEW, AUDIT]
  build: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX]

arms:
  - {id: a0_bare, label: A0, task_types: [all], toggles: {loa_mount: false}, phases: [BARE], effort: high,
     took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a1_full, label: A1, task_types: [all], toggles: {}, took_effect: [all_phases_present, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a2_no_sprint_plan, label: A2, task_types: [build], toggles: {sprint_plan: false},
     phases: [IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, FIX, AUDIT, FIX],
     took_effect: [no_plan_phase, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a3_one_voice, label: A3, task_types: [all], toggles: {companion_voice: false}, took_effect: [one_voice_planned, integrity_clean]}
  - {id: a4_no_gates, label: A4, task_types: [build], toggles: {gates: false},
     phases: [PLAN, IMPLEMENT],
     took_effect: [no_gate_phases, enforce_env_false, applicability_refused, integrity_clean]}   # build only: on a review-catch task the gates are the task (DEC-0400)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# claude-ablation-stub.sh — wraps evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub.sh for the
     3	# cycle-130 bats (run-arms.bats, arm-toggles.bats). No model call.
     4	#
     5	#   STUB_COST_USD      the result event's total_cost_usd (default: the base stub's
     6	#                      canned transcript is used unchanged)
     7	#   STUB_FULL_ENV_FILE the complete environment (`env`) is written there
     8	#   STUB_CONC_DIR      concurrency probe: each call registers itself in the dir
     9	#                      for STUB_SLEEP seconds and appends the number of calls
    10	#                      running at its start to <dir>.log
    11	#   STUB_SLEEP         seconds to stay registered (default 0)
    12	set -euo pipefail
    13	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    14	BASE="$HERE/../claude-stub.sh"
    15	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--version" ]]; then exec "$BASE" --version; fi
    16	
    17	if [[ -n "${STUB_FULL_ENV_FILE:-}" ]]; then env > "$STUB_FULL_ENV_FILE"; fi
    18	if [[ -n "${STUB_CONC_DIR:-}" ]]; then
    19	  mkdir -p "$STUB_CONC_DIR"
    20	  : > "$STUB_CONC_DIR/$$"
    21	  ls "$STUB_CONC_DIR" | wc -l | tr -d ' ' >> "$STUB_CONC_DIR.log"
    22	  sleep "${STUB_SLEEP:-0}"
    23	  rm -f "$STUB_CONC_DIR/$$"
    24	fi
    25	if [[ -n "${STUB_COST_USD:-}" ]]; then
    26	  ev="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/stub-events.XXXXXX")"
    27	  cat > "$ev" <<EVENTS
    28	{"type":"system","subtype":"init","model":"claude-sonnet-5"}
    29	{"type":"assistant","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"review.md","content":"r"}}]}}
    30	{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"duration_ms":1000,"num_turns":2,"result":"done","total_cost_usd":${STUB_COST_USD},"usage":{"input_tokens":10,"output_tokens":5},"modelUsage":{"claude-sonnet-5-20260401":{"inputTokens":10,"outputTokens":5,"costUSD":${STUB_COST_USD}}}}
    31	EVENTS
    32	  export STUB_EVENTS_FILE="$ev"
    33	fi
    34	exec "$BASE" "$@"
    35	# suite-lib.bash — fixture-suite builders for validate-suite.bats and freeze.bats
    36	# (cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.11). Sourced by the bats files; the templates are
    37	# the two committed smoke tasks, so the fixtures follow the real schema.
    38	#
    39	#   make_task <root> <group> <id> <type>   copy a smoke task to <root>/<group>/<id>
    40	#                                          as <type> (build types from smoke-build-01,
    41	#                                          review-catch from smoke-review-01)
    42	#   make_full_suite <root>                 four tasks of each type under tasks/
    43	
    44	SMOKE_ROOT="${SMOKE_ROOT:-$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke}"
    45	
    46	make_task() {
    47	  local root="$1" group="$2" id="$3" type="$4" src
    48	  case "$type" in review-catch) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-review-01" ;; *) src="$SMOKE_ROOT/smoke-build-01" ;; esac
    49	  mkdir -p "$root/$group"
    50	  cp -a "$src" "$root/$group/$id"
    51	  local ty="$root/$group/$id/task.yaml"
    52	  ID="$id" TY="$type" yq -i '.id = strenv(ID) | .type = strenv(TY)' "$ty"
    53	  if [[ "$type" != "review-catch" ]]; then
    54	    FX="$group/$id/fixture" yq -i '.fixture = strenv(FX)' "$ty"
    55	  fi
    56	  if [[ "$type" == "refactor" ]]; then
    57	    printf 'def test_structure():\n    assert True\n' > "$root/$group/$id/hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"
    58	    yq -i '.structural_check = "hidden/tests/test_structure_check.py"' "$ty"
    59	  fi
    60	}
    61	
    62	make_full_suite() {
    63	  local root="$1" ty i
    64	  for ty in feature-build bug-fix refactor review-catch; do
    65	    for i in 1 2 3 4; do make_task "$root" tasks "$ty-0$i" "$ty"; done
    66	  done
    67	}

#   failed rows, run_cap = --run-cap (default evals.ablation.run_cap_usd in
#   .loa.config.yaml, else 12) reserved per running trial, and est_next = the

#   else the pooled mean, else the suite's ab.cost_hint (or cost_hint), else 5.0.
#   While the reservation alone blocks the launch it waits for a running trial;
#   when spent + est_next > max it cuts: no further launches, running trials

def test_ledger_rows_carry_resolution_transport_and_estimate_flags(catalog):
    row = create_ledger_entry(
        trace_id="t", agent="a", provider="openai", model="gpt-5.5-2026-04-23",
        input_tokens=1000, output_tokens=100, reasoning_tokens=0, latency_ms=1,
        config=catalog, usage_source="actual",
    )
    assert row["pricing_source"] == "config" and row["pricing_resolution"] == "dated"
    assert row["cost_micro_usd"] > 0 and "cost_estimated" not in row

    est = create_ledger_entry(
        trace_id="t", agent="a", provider="anthropic", model="claude-headless",
        input_tokens=1000, output_tokens=100, reasoning_tokens=0, latency_ms=1,
        config=catalog, usage_source="estimated", resolved_model="fable", transport="cli:claude",
    )
    assert est["pricing_source"] == "config" and est["pricing_resolution"] == "hop"
    assert est["cost_estimated"] is True
    assert est["resolved_model"] == "fable" and est["transport"] == "cli:claude"

    unknown = create_ledger_entry(
        trace_id="t", agent="a", provider="openai", model="nope-9000",
        input_tokens=1000, output_tokens=100, reasoning_tokens=0, latency_ms=1,
        config=catalog, usage_source="actual",
    )
    assert unknown["pricing_source"] == "unknown" and unknown["cost_micro_usd"] == 0
    assert "pricing_resolution" not in unknown and "cost_estimated" not in unknown


def test_resolved_model_fallback_prices_a_row_whose_model_is_unknown(catalog):
    row = create_ledger_entry(

        input_tokens=1000, output_tokens=100, reasoning_tokens=0, latency_ms=1,
        config=catalog, usage_source="actual", resolved_model="claude-fable-5-1",
    )
    assert row["pricing_source"] == "config" and row["pricing_resolution"] == "exact"
    assert row["resolved_model"] == "claude-fable-5-1"

content.text:
I found 17 issues across the six scripts, the suite yaml and the tests; the worst is that `integrity_clean` passes a sandbox that was tampered with and then had its checksums rewritten. The workspace snapshot is incomplete: it has no `grimoires/`, no `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` and no `tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, and the copy had lost its exec bits. To run anything I copied the tree to `$HOME/review-y/head`, because `/tmp` is mounted noexec. There I ran `regen.sh` with jq 1.7.1 (the system jq is 1.6). After that, all 39 tests in `took-effect.bats` and `ablation-row.bats` pass, and all 6 in `spend.bats` pass. I could not run `freeze.bats` or `validate-suite.bats` because the files they need are missing from the snapshot.

## High / medium

1. **head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266** — `integrity_clean` never compares the recorded `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256` with the sandbox's `checksums.json`. A mismatch just drops the "(matches checksums.json)" suffix and the rule still returns 0. So an agent that edits a mounted `.claude/` file and rewrites its entry in `sandbox/.claude/checksums.json` passes. Lines 239–240 only check that the recorded hash exists. Verified: I tampered `.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md` in the a1-build copy and re-hashed its entry, and the output was `integrity_clean OK 5 manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 8c267cb13e8a`, then `arm a1_full: OK`, exit 0. The recorded hash in `pipeline.json` sits outside the sandbox and is the only trustworthy anchor, but it is ignored. Deleting a file together with its manifest entry, or adding unlisted `.claude/` files, also passes. `took-effect.bats:164-173` does this re-hashing deliberately, which hides the problem.

2. **head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:354-356** — the `--batch-dir` walk (`find -maxdepth 4 -name meta`) doesn't skip `sandbox/`, so a `meta/pipeline.json` written by the agent counts as a run. This goes against the "never from sandbox/" rule (DEC-0413). Verified:
   - `runs/a1-build/sandbox/meta/pipeline.json` containing `{}` aborts the whole batch with exit 2 ("no arm for …/sandbox").
   - Adding `sandbox/meta/arm` makes it a forged extra run: "took-effect: 11 runs, 0 failed".

3. **head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:18, head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:19** — both `setup()` functions run `cp -a "$FX/runs"`, but the PR doesn't add `fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`; only `regen.sh` creates it. CI runs `bats evals/tests/` (`bats-tests.yml:221`), so on a fresh checkout all 39 of these tests fail in setup. This may just be the review snapshot leaving out a large directory, so confirm it is actually committed.

4. **Assertions that can never fail (bats `set -e` ignores a failing left side of `&&` and any `! cmd` that is not the last command).** I confirmed both behaviours with small bats probes.
   - head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:147 — `[ "$status" -eq 1 ] && line … | grep -q 'REVIEW and AUDIT share session'`. The REVIEW==AUDIT case is never actually checked.
   - head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:112, 115, 118, 140 — the status-enum, task_type-enum, "degraded without degraded_reason" and "graded build row has no hidden_tests" checks are all no-ops.
   - head/evals/tests/freeze.bats:38 (`! grep -qv '^[0-9a-f]\{64\}  tasks/'`) and :79 (`! grep -q '  smoke/'`) — both no-ops.
   - head/evals/tests/spend.bats:83-88 (SP-6) — this test is vacuous rather than a no-op. It asserts the suite yaml says 1500, then checks only `reserve_usd == 250`, which equals the hardcoded fallback. It never checks `cap_usd`, so a broken yq lookup would still pass. The `.loa.config.yaml` value would also take precedence.

5. **Exit code 1 instead of 2 when an option's value is missing.** `VAR="${2:-}"; shift 2` with no value fails `shift` under `set -e`, so the script exits 1. That code means "rule FAIL", "bad row" or "drift" in these scripts, so a driver would misread a usage error as a real failure. Verified for each script: `took-effect.sh --suite-file F --run-dir` gives 1, as do `spend.sh --cap`, `ablation-row.sh --validate`, `freeze.sh --root` and `validate-suite.sh --root`. The lines are:
   - took-effect.sh:69-72
   - spend.sh:49,55,56
   - ablation-row.sh:73-81
   - freeze.sh:43
   - validate-suite.sh:62,65
   - fingerprint.sh:44-46: `${2:?…}` also exits 1, while the header (line 28) documents 2.

6. **head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:139-140, 157-158, 273-276** — several rules pass when `pipeline.json` can't be read. A failed `jq` leaves `n` empty, and `[[ "" -eq 0 ]]` is true; an empty label list or task type also counts as a pass. Verified with a truncated `pipeline.json`:
   - `no_plan_phase OK no PLAN record`
   - `no_gate_phases OK`
   - `applicability_refused OK applicable:  in task_types ["build"]` (the task type is blank)

   The overall verdict was still FAIL, but only because `integrity_clean` failed.

7. **head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285** — `{name, label, …}` uses `label`, which is a reserved word in jq 1.6, so the script fails to compile there. Verified: jq-1.6 reports "syntax error … line 58" and no row is written. `took-effect.sh` works under 1.6. CI's ubuntu-latest ships jq 1.7, but nothing states or checks the jq version requirement.

## Low

8. **head/evals/harness/freeze.sh:69** — `find "$d" -type f` skips symlinks and doesn't descend into symlinked directories. A symlinked file under `tasks/` is never hashed, so its target can change without `--check` noticing.
9. **head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133** — the "stopped early, prefix is OK" branch also accepts `running`, but the header (lines 18-19) lists only cap_failure, agent_error and interrupted.
10. **head/evals/harness/spend.sh:152** — the ledger cost reads only `cost_micro_usd`. `pipeline-run.sh:771` also accepts a `cost_usd` fallback for the same kind of rows, and spend.sh would count those as $0 without listing them as skipped. More generally, ledger rows with a missing or unparseable `ts` are skipped (lines 148-155), which makes the spend total lower than it should be.
11. **head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:55 vs 137** — the docs say `--allow-ungraded` accepts rows "whose grade fields are all null". The code actually skips the graded check entirely and never verifies the fields are null. Separately, blank lines are counted in the "N rows valid" message (lines 95-96, 152).
12. **head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:83** — `exclusion.statuses` includes `degraded`, but that isn't a status value: ablation-row.sh:88 has seven statuses, and `degraded` is a separate boolean field.
13. **head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:326** — `(e or {}).get` raises AttributeError when a `hidden/manifest.json` entry isn't an object (e.g. a string). The result is "validator crashed" (exit 2) instead of a reported violation.
14. **head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:89 vs freeze.sh:69** — dot-named task directories are never validated (the `*/` glob skips them), but freeze still hashes them into the manifest.
15. **head/evals/harness/validate-suite.sh:368** — the message prefix is doubled: it prints `fixture path rule: fixture path rule: <dir> holds…`.
16. **head/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh:83** — `git -C DIR rev-parse HEAD` on a subdirectory of another repository returns that repository's HEAD, not `none` as documented for a non-git tree.

These checked out: `MANIFEST.json` matches what `regen.sh` writes (`jq -S` diff is empty), the run_ids match the regenerated runs, and the live suite's BARE caps add up (170 turns / 70 min). My working copy is in `$HOME/review-y/`; nothing under `/workspace/pr` was modified.

content.text:
I found 18 defects. The worst is a sandbox escape: anything the agent writes into the sandbox's `.git` runs on the host. Several tests also contain assertions that can never fail.

**How I ran things:** `/tmp` is mounted noexec, so I ran copies from `$TMPDIR` (`/workspace/.eval/tmp`). The checkout also dropped the 100755 modes, so I restored them on the copy. `/workspace/pr` was not modified and the scratch copies are deleted. With the system jq 1.6, 48 of 52 tests fail. With jq 1.7.1 all 52 pass. With the real `lib/sandbox-mount.sh` in place of the stub, only the 4 stub-specific tests fail. I confirmed findings 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 by reproducing them.

### High

1. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:783`** (also `:784`, `:787`, and `sgit` at `:446-449`): the agent can run code on the host.
   - In container mode `.git` sits inside the read-write `/workspace` mount. After IMPLEMENT and each FIX, the driver runs `git add -A`, `git commit` and `git bundle` on the host.
   - `env -i GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` does not cover the repo's own `.git/config` or `.git/hooks`. So `core.fsmonitor`, a `filter.*` driver, `core.hooksPath` or an executable hook all run as the operator, outside the container.
   - **Reproduced:** a stub phase wrote `.git/hooks/post-commit`, and the driver's snapshot commit ran it on the host, creating a marker file outside the sandbox.
   - **Fix:** run git with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=` and ignore repo-local config, or take the snapshots inside the container.

2. **`head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:668-669`**: the "allowlist … the in-container env equals it" test checks nothing.
   - Both `! grep …` lines are mid-test, and bash `set -e` ignores failures of `!`-negated commands. Only line 670 is enforced.
   - **Reproduced:** I added `GH_TOKEN` and `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` to `PASS_KEYS` so both reach the container. The test still passes.

3. **`head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:610`**: the "meta boundary" test never checks for the arm id.
   - The `! grep -rqF "$arm" sandbox snapshots transcripts eval` line is mid-loop, so it cannot fail.
   - **Reproduced:** with the arm id written to `sandbox/.eval/arm-leak`, the test still passes.

### Medium

4. **`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:513`** (called via `pipeline-run.sh:489` and `lib_call` at `:402`): code from the evaluated tree runs on the host with every secret in scope.
   - If `br` is not on the host PATH, `init_sandbox_beads` runs `bash "$ws/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh"`. That script comes from the mounted `--source-tree` (possibly a PR).
   - It runs on the host with the driver's full environment: `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `GH_TOKEN`, AWS keys and so on. `lib_call` does not scrub the environment.
   - This contradicts the trust-boundary comment (`pipeline-run.sh:125-126`) and the env allowlist. The trust-boundary test (`pipeline-run.bats:251`) only scans 4 files, skips `lib/sandbox-mount.sh`, and only looks for `source`/`.`, not `bash <path>`.

5. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:860-862`**: infrastructure failures are recorded as the agent's fault.
   - Any non-zero exit becomes `agent_error` (exit 1). That includes `docker run`'s own errors (125: daemon down, container name in use) and `timeout`'s 126/127 (CLI missing).
   - The header (`:99-100`) says a missing CLI or docker is `infrastructure_error` (exit 2).
   - **Reproduced:** with `LOA_EVAL_CONTAINER_CLAUDE_BIN=/no/such/claude` the run ends `{"status":"agent_error","reason":"phase PLAN exited 127"}`, exit 1.

6. **`head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:311`**: the A0 test does not check that `.claude/` or `CLAUDE.md` are absent.
   - In `[ ! -e .claude ] && [ ! -e CLAUDE.md ] && [ ! -e grimoires ]` mid-test, only the last element can fail the test. A failing earlier element just stops the `&&` list without tripping `set -e`.
   - **Reproduced:** with `.claude/skills` and `CLAUDE.md` created in the A0 sandbox, the test passes.

7. **Other assertions in `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats` that never fail:**
   - Mid-test `!` lines: 237 (`PATH=/evil` filter), 332 (`effort:` stripped), 339 (no `--effort` on A1), 391 and 392 (no "hidden" or defect key in prompts), 652, 726 (token absent from stub logs).
   - Line 394 sits in a loop, so only the last arm id (`a8_no_ceremonies`) is checked.
   - `&&` chains whose earlier elements are ignored: 201, 202, 204, 209, 294, 390, 548.
   - Line 157 is a tautology (`[ $((30+60+2*40)) -eq 170 ]`).
   - The test at 241-246 ("LOA_EVAL_MOUNT_LIB is ignored") is vacuous: no code reads that variable.

8. **jq 1.7+ is required but never checked.** The preflight at `pipeline-run.sh:167` only checks that jq exists.
   - `$label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6, so these programs fail to compile there: `pipeline-run.sh:702/708`, `:816/826`, `:881-882` and `sandbox-mount.sh:462/467`.
   - Every phase then aborts as `infrastructure_error`. Debian bookworm (the base of `Dockerfile.ablation`) and Ubuntu 22.04 ship jq 1.6.
   - **Fix:** rename the variable (e.g. `$lbl`) or add a version check.

9. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:773-778`** (also `:713`, `:769`): the driver follows agent-controlled symlinks on the host.
   - It reads and `cp`s `sandbox/.eval/*.jsonl` and `a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-*.json` without checking for symlinks.
   - From the container, the agent can point these at host paths. The host file's contents then get copied into the grader-visible `eval/`, or `wc -l` blocks on something like `/dev/zero`.

10. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:690`**: gate phases can read the implementer's transcripts.
    - In container mode the one per-run HOME is shared by all phases. The CLI's session store (`~/.claude/projects/-workspace/*.jsonl`) holds the implementer's full transcripts.
    - So in A1, REVIEW and AUDIT can read them, which weakens the separation A6 (`context_resets`) is measured against.

### Low

11. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:595`** (with `:718`): the price cache never works. `price_for` runs inside `$(...)`, so the `PRICE_CACHE` update is lost and `pricing.py` is called every phase. This contradicts "fetched once per model" (`:91`).

12. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:586`** (not verified: `pricing.py` is not in this tree): `python3 -I` puts neither the cwd nor the script's directory on `sys.path`, so the `cd .claude/adapters` has no effect. If `pricing.py` imports `loa_cheval.*`, it fails silently and the watchdog stays off in production. The tests always set `LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON`, so this path is never exercised.

13. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:85`**: the header says the image ships codex 0.137.0, but `head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:25` pins `CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1`.

14. **`head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:77-79`**: the comment says the sandbox always gets the beads opt-out marker. But `init_sandbox_beads` (`sandbox-mount.sh:504-509`) runs on the host and uses `br` if the host has it. The sandbox then gets a `.beads` database that the image (which has no `br`) cannot use, so arms are not run "alike".

15. **`head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:19-20`**: the `brbuild` stage is unpinned (`rust:1-bookworm`) and never used. Line 77 says beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io, so building with the legacy builder (`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`) fails.

16. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:50`**: the header documents `index.json` keys as `IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2`. The code at `:788-789` writes lowercase keys plus `base`.

17. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:477`**: `>> "$WS/.git/info/exclude"` assumes git's templates created `.git/info`. Without them the driver aborts. A `mkdir -p` is missing.

18. **`head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:167`**: `python3` (needed by `ENV_SHIM`) is not in the required-tools check.

if [[ "$rel" == /* ]]; then [[ -d "$rel" ]] && { printf '%s' "$rel"; return 0; }; return 1; fi
  for c in "$TASK_DIR/$rel" "$SUITE_ROOT/$rel" "$REPO_ROOT/$rel" "$REPO_ROOT/evals/fixtures/$rel" "$SOURCE_TREE/evals/fixtures/$rel"; do
    [[ -d "$c" ]] && { (cd "$c" && pwd); return 0; }
  done
  return 1
}
sgit() {  # git on the sandbox repo, isolated from the operator's git config
  env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$META" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 LC_ALL=C \
    git -C "$WS" "$@"
}

if [[ "$KIND" == build ]]; then
  fx_rel="$(jq -r '.fixture // ""' <<<"$TASK_JSON")"
  done
  if [[ $rc -eq 124 ]] || { [[ $rc -eq 137 ]] && [[ $elapsed_ms -ge $(( tsec * 1000 )) ]]; }; then timed_out=true; fi

  local snap="" verdict=null skill effort_req
  if [[ "$INTERRUPTED" -eq 0 ]] && { [[ "$name" == IMPLEMENT ]] || [[ "$name" == FIX ]]; }; then
    sgit add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $label" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    snap="$(sgit rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$snap" ]]; then
      sgit bundle create "$SNAPS/$label.bundle" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      SNAPSHOTS_JSON="$(jq -c --arg k "$(printf '%s' "$label" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" --arg v "$snap" '.[$k] = $v' <<<"$SNAPSHOTS_JSON")"
      jq -n --argjson s "$SNAPSHOTS_JSON" --arg base "$BASE_COMMIT" '$s + {base: $base}' > "$SNAPS/index.json"
    fi
init_sandbox_beads() {
  local ws="$1" title="${2:-}"
  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "init_sandbox_beads: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$title" ]] || title="eval task"
  local br="${LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN:-br}"
  if command -v "$br" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ( cd "$ws" && "$br" init --prefix bd --no-daemon >/dev/null 2>&1 && "$br" create "$title" --type task --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 ) \
      || { _sm_err "init_sandbox_beads: br init/create failed in $ws"; return 2; }
    _sm_evidence beads "br"
